A1.justification: Both PDFs describe THOR and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Renamed components and relocated appendix material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical and coding benchmark evaluations, component ablations, execution-success analysis, and inference token measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds candidate-selection comparisons, repair-strategy evaluations, execution diagnostics, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds an optional hybrid selection strategy using external reward scores to distinguish candidates with identical execution pass rates. The core TIRGen, hierarchical RL, and suffix-repair procedures remain unchanged; actor/critic and trajectory-level become generator/refiner and episode-level.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same mathematical and coding benchmarks and the same training sources: DAPO17k, DeepMath103k, DeepScaler40k, and ToRL28k. Added analyses concern retained tasks and data rather than new domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands comparison beyond single-path inference to self-consistency, InternLM2-1.8B-RM, Qwen2.5-Math-PRM, and hybrid selection. Table 1 adds ARTIST-7B and TATA-7B and removes OpenAI o1. New repair comparisons also evaluate action-only repair and full replanning against suffix repair.

E3.justification: Table 2 replaces the N=4/8 sweep with comparisons at N=8. New appendix evaluations introduce repair controls, execution diagnostics, and latency/FPS measurements under vLLM. Table 1 changes the Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B baseline to code use. Main benchmark metrics and context limits remain unchanged; newly disclosed sampling settings do not establish changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.2 compares action-only, suffix, and full-replanning repairs and examines explicit versus emergent correction through failed/successful calls and execution pass rates. Runtime analysis extends the earlier token-cost analysis. The original component ablations and case studies remain, while the N=4/8 scaling analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Avg@4 reporting and the same chi-square analysis, including chi-square=336.3 and p=4.09×10^-75. No new uncertainty-reporting practice, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial selector, repair, execution-diagnostic, and runtime results and revises Table 1 entries. For example, THOR-1.5B's reported MATH500 score changes from 79.0 to 78.2 and Minerva Math from 36.0 to 38.2. New hybrid-selection averages are 64.4 and 84.3. BoN@4 results disappear, while the main THOR-7B and THOR-Thinking-8B averages remain 61.2 and 79.8.

T1.justification: Section 2.3.2 explicitly defines the normalized episode-level and step-level advantages, including new Equation 9; v1 used these advantage symbols without those definitions. The trajectory factorization and principal objectives are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Contribution 4 changes from achieving SOTA to achieving competitive mathematical results, modestly narrowing that statement. However, SOTA wording remains in the abstract and introduction, and the principal methodological and generalization claims are retained.

C2.justification: v3 interprets hybrid-selection gains as complementarity between execution feedback and learned rewards and discusses reward-model training-coverage limitations. Appendix C.2 distinguishes code errors from preceding reasoning inconsistencies when motivating repair alternatives. The original limitations concerning other tools and larger models are retained after relocation.

D1.justification: Appendix D supplies previously unspecified sampling temperatures, top-k/top-p settings, backtracking lengths of 100/500, and failed-step downsampling rules. Section 3.3 clarifies that BoN candidates omit self-correction. These are additional implementation disclosures, not evidence that existing experiments changed. Hardware, prompts, and the promised future code/data release remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for ARTIST, TATA, InternLM2, self-consistency, ToolRL, and Luo et al. (2026), while removing Search-o1 and Mulberry. Positioning expands around reward-based selection and tool learning, but the existing tool-free/tool-integrated research framing remains.

P1.justification: Terminology is standardized and portions of the introduction and methodology are polished. Limitations move to Appendix E, social impact becomes the main-text Ethics Statement, and acknowledgments are added. The main narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The empirical displays expand substantially: Table 2 becomes a selector comparison, new Tables 5–6 present repair and execution analyses, and the former token-cost table gains runtime/FPS columns. Figures 1–3 receive revised labels, Figure 4 gains numerical annotations, and Figure 6 changes an axis range. Existing prompt and case-study figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 better supports its inference choices through competing selectors and repair controls, adds measured runtime beyond token-count proxies, and fills useful implementation gaps. These strengthen the existing study without fundamentally changing its evidence base. The loss of BoN@4 results reduces scaling detail, and equal candidate counts alone do not establish equal total compute across reward-model methods, but the net gains in validation and reproducibility are clear.
